title: Keep track of the change
intro: Make Change Stack easier to review without losing what it can do. I focused on understanding the change, checking its code and tracking progress. My assumption: keeping the layer, file, explanation and review state together takes extra effort.
rows: Summary points share a broad range. Expanding also moves the code.
Keep the original summary wording visible. Expand in place, with a line link beside each statement. Reading and navigation become separate actions; the whole function remains available.
Layers and files are separate. Following a guard leaves a return trip to remember.
Nest files under their layer. Inspect guard opens the dependency; Return restores the caller and position. This keeps one wide code pane; a side-by-side option would need more horizontal space.
Keep frequent file actions beside the filename and display controls beside the diff. Put secondary actions in Tools. That adds a click; I’d check whether people can find them.
File and layer totals need a clear scope.
Start with This file and keep Entire layer one click away. Counts follow the scope: access.ts has 3 messages; its layer has 15. The diff stays in place.
Seen, viewed and submitted mean different things.
The source already has seen and viewed controls. I added a file count and immediate Undo. Navigation leaves progress alone; summary seen and Submit keep their own meanings.
tradeoff: Context takes space from the diff; Focus gives it back. Precise highlights can distract from surrounding branches. Inspect + Return means switching views. Status-first comments need testing with open findings; this sample has one resolved thread.
validation: The header, merged state, layer order, counts, complexity labels, J/K and Focus remain. Comments retain their metadata and expand in place; a separate line link opens code. Gray marks selection; orange highlights linked code.
next: Trace the workspace guard, explain its checks, return and mark the file viewed. Compare both versions, varying the order; note missed checks and lost position. Then try more dependencies and open findings. Check how new commits affect links and viewed progress.
scope: Observations and assumptions from using this PR, not developer research. Seven of 52 diffs at commit 23cdac2; manually mapped links; one paraphrased finding, with two reply bodies omitted. Secondary workflows are previews. Submit is disabled for the merged PR. Work exceeded the 1–2 hour brief. Paper requires sign-in.
